# Phase 34.4 native-host scripted answers

Use equivalent briefs under `claude -p` and `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`.
When the inherited approval mode is automatic review, use `codex exec --approve-for-me`
instead: this CLI option itself selects workspace-write plus automatic review and
is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox`. Record the resolved authority and each review.
Each arm starts in a fresh scratch repository. Record the exact executable, version,
argv, source commit, plugin manifest digest, scratch identity, and `AuthorityEnvelope`.
The authority is filesystem `workspace-write`, network `inherited`, approvals `inherited`.
Permission or sandbox bypass options are forbidden. Do not widen inherited authority,
write outside scratch, contact product remotes, or perform unrecorded external actions.

## Common answers

Project: greenfield-proof. TypeScript library/CLI; npm; mobile: none; non-Blade.
Audience: developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI. The first
release exports a typed greeting and CLI with passing tests. No authentication,
external service, deployment, or product remote. Preserve unknowns explicitly.
Use the installed greenfield and roadmap plugin contracts and library-cli manifest.
Read the templates and references; do not substitute invented config keys or omit
promised homes. Existing brownfield homes and generated harness blocks are immutable.

## First invocation: proposal only

Read the fixture and run only the named `roadmap config capabilities --json`
compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including
`roadmap init --help`, before approval. Read static source or top-level help for
syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one
JSON object `{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[],"commands":[],"gates":{}}` with
concrete populated values. Its gates have exactly lint, types, unit, integration,
build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has
a reason. Validate those keys before requesting approval. Do not emit an approval
event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

## Driver approval and execution

The driver checks the complete proposal and unchanged initial tree, then records the
approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.
Resume the same host session with that exact standalone input. The prior proposal
is the approved path/command allowlist; do not bundle new instructions into approval.
If the proposal fails validation, issue no approval and capture the failed arm.
If any preapproval mutation occurs, STOP immediately without deleting or reverting
it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

Execute only approved operations. Emit `WRITE:` diagnostics for traceability, but
success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately with explicit `cd '<scratch>' &&` cwd evidence.
Use the host envelope below for suite/build/type commands; retain both the exact
portable configured command and the wrapped native invocation with its real exit. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

Required empty artifacts include PRD, both ADRs, CODE-STYLE, architecture index,
UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff
to approved gaps. Test migrated docs/roadmap, explicit root override, and ambiguous
dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

## Repeated invocation

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result
`{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only if the audit
finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.
Pass `sourceRoot`, `invocationBaseCommit`, and `sourceSnapshotSha256` in every
observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.
Use `greenfield-native-observer.py` in the same directory to launch each request;
it checks source before and after and records transient filesystem mutations.
Keep `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so read-only Git inspection does not refresh the index.
Propose scratch-local `.npm-cache/` and `.npm-logs/` paths when npm needs them;
include those settings in approved commands. Do not commit inside native fixtures.

After each stage finishes, run `greenfield-native-driver.mjs capture <host>
<stage-directory>` before resuming. The driver copies the native session and
checks identity, authority, command events, snapshots, and proposal structure.
Use separate `proposal`, `execution`, and `rerun` directories below each arm's
`dry-runs/evidence/` directory; never overwrite a failed attempt. Supply `arm.json`
with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

## Host build envelope

Resolve `/home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild` and its canonical path before launch;
bind its SHA-256, default limits, and permitted host effects as `gateWrapper` in
arm metadata and every stage request. Use the same binding for all four arms.
Keep `capbuild` out of consumer `gateCommands`; it is a host execution requirement,
not consumer tooling. For each build, type, unit, integration, and emit command,
propose its actual execution separately using this exact envelope:

```sh
cd '<scratch>' && /home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild --env npm_config_cache=<scratch>/.npm-cache --env npm_config_logs_dir=<scratch>/.npm-logs <configured-command>
```

Define `<scratch>` as the absolute observed fixture root and `<configured-command>`
as its exact portable gate binding. Use literal absolute cache/log values. Select
portable gate commands without shell operators or assignment prefixes; use
`env TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 node --import tsx roadmap/lib/emit.ts` for the fixture emit
gate so transform caching stays disabled across the systemd environment boundary.
Do not change memory/swap/heap/slice defaults, disable locks, add arbitrary environment
options, or run an unwrapped suite inside a compound verification command. Keep
config check and the selected catalog comparator as separate ordinary invocations.

Permit only capbuild's inherited host-control effects outside the consumer tree:
transient user-systemd units and `/run/user/<uid>/capbuild-locks`, where `<uid>` is
the current numeric user id recorded by the driver. These are safety metadata;
they do not authorize any additional consumer path. Record the actual wrapper
command/output/exit and verify the bound executable digest remains unchanged.
The observer clears ambient capbuild, Node, and forwarded test overrides before
launch and records the cleared variable names without exposing their values.

name: using-zeroh-greenfield
description: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill.
---

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

name: using-zeroh-greenfield
description: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill.
---

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

---
name: greenfield-init
description: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
---

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, run only that named roadmap command; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
and roadmap configuration before requesting approval.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Ask for the exact response `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN`.

STOP before any write or generator run unless that exact response follows the
complete proposal. Do not interpret partial agreement as approval. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
Treat this gate as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs`; other approval interpretation is honor-system.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.
=====ARCH README
# Archetype manifest contract

## Generator
One fenced block containing a literal generator command.

## Post-steps
Exact approved edits after generation.

## File tree
One fenced, non-empty two-level tree.

## Conventions delta
Only archetype-specific additions to the shared conventions.

## testConventions
At least two literal commands or patterns.

## designHomes
The architecture and UX pointers consumed by the roadmap.

## Verify
Exactly one fenced, single-line exit-code command. Keep observations and dates
only in `VERIFY-RECORD-2026-09.md`.
=====LIBCLI
## Generator
```sh
npx create-vite@^8 my-lib --template vanilla-ts
```

Source: https://vite.dev/guide/. Vite is MIT, tier `Allowed anywhere`.

## Post-steps
Install `tsup: ^8.5` and `@types/node`, and include `node` in the TypeScript
`types` list. tsup is sourced from https://tsup.egoist.dev/; it is MIT and
`Allowed anywhere`. Set package.json `exports` to `./dist/index.js`, `bin` to
`./dist/cli.js`, and `files` to `dist`. Configure `tsup.config.ts` with
`entry: ['src/index.ts', 'src/cli.ts']`, `format: ['esm']`, and `dts: true`.
Set the package.json `build` script to `tsup`.
Give the CLI a Node shebang and a stable `--help` path. Add at least one
`node:test` file for the public API, then run the tsup build before Verify.

## File tree
```text
my-lib/
my-lib/package.json
my-lib/src/index.ts
my-lib/src/cli.ts
my-lib/tsup.config.ts
```

## Conventions delta
Keep the reusable API in `src/index.ts` and the thin executable adapter in
`src/cli.ts`; publish only built artifacts through `exports`, `bin`, and `files`.

## testConventions
Use `node --test` for behavior and `node dist/cli.js --help` as the built CLI
smoke check. Test runner source: https://nodejs.org/api/test.html.

## designHomes
Set `designHomes.architecture.home` to `docs/architecture.md` and
`designHomes.ux.canon` to `docs/ux-canon.md`.

## Verify
```sh
test -f my-lib/package.json && test -f my-lib/src/index.ts && test -f my-lib/src/cli.ts && test -f my-lib/tsup.config.ts && (cd my-lib && npm run build && node --test && node dist/cli.js --help && node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --project-root .)
```

```text
my-lib/
my-lib/package.json
my-lib/src/index.ts
my-lib/src/cli.ts
my-lib/tsup.config.ts

```

===== stack-decision
---
name: stack-decision
description: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling.
---

# Stack decision

Load `references/matrices.md`. Determine which matrices apply from the approved
PRD answers, then present every row in each applicable matrix unchanged.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, leave repository changes to `greenfield-init` or `brownfield-audit`, and return only `StackDecisionOutput` here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-30.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Selection

Ask exactly one selection question per applicable matrix.
Do not preselect any option before the user answers.
Present the backend matrix ONLY when the PRD answers name an API.

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.
If matrix evidence is unavailable, PRD answers conflict, or the reason is unconfirmed, STOP with `status: unresolved` and name the missing evidence or conflicting answers. Treat selection and STOP behavior as honor-system.

## Callers and ownership

Accept calls from `greenfield-init` for new repositories and from `brownfield-audit` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting. Keep matrices and ADR decision content in this skill and `references/matrices.md`.

Return both stack ADR decisions without implementing design or token values; delegate those values to the selected design system or `zeroh-design`.

## Output

Return one `StackDecisionOutput` containing one object per applicable matrix:

```json
{"status":"decided|unresolved","decisions":[{"adrPath":"docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md|docs/adr/0002-design-system.md","matrix":"<matrix-heading>","options":["<exact-presented-row>"],"selected":"<named-option>","reason":"<confirmed-reason>","consequences":["<consequence>"],"revisitConditions":["<measurable-condition>"],"rulingDate":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]}
```

Define `YYYY-MM-DD` as the decision's ISO calendar date, `<matrix-heading>` as the literal heading in `references/matrices.md`, and every other placeholder as non-empty text copied or confirmed during selection. On STOP, return `{"status":"unresolved","decisions":[]}` plus the named conflict in the surrounding response.

Accumulate every applicable stack decision in the single
`docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md`: create a labeled Options group for each presented
matrix, preserve all of its sourced rows, and add one dated ruling per group.
Never replace an earlier group's alternatives or ruling when the next matrix is
answered. Populate `docs/adr/0002-design-system.md` separately from only the
design-system options and ruling.

Add the confirmed consequences and measurable revisit conditions for every
group. Do not write either ADR until the calling workflow's approval gate has
passed.
Treat preservation of earlier groups as honor-system. Treat the no-write rule as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` when called inside native initialization; otherwise it is honor-system.
===== matrices
# Stack matrices

Present only the applicable sections and preserve every row when asking for a choice.

## Web
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js + shadcn/ui | Integrated full-stack React and accessible primitives | Framework conventions add coupling | Product needs routing, rendering, and server seams | Registry components remain source-owned | https://nextjs.org/docs |
| Vite + React | Small, fast client toolchain | Backend and routing need separate choices | Client-rendered app has independent services | React components move between Vite applications | https://vite.dev/guide |
| SvelteKit | Concise components and integrated routing | Smaller React-library ecosystem | Team prefers Svelte and server rendering | Svelte components share within Svelte projects | https://svelte.dev/docs/kit |

## Mobile
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flutter + shadcn_flutter | One Dart UI across supported platforms | Native integrations need platform bridges | Consistent cross-platform UI is primary | Shared Dart widgets and token names | shadcn_flutter |
| Kotlin/Compose/Material 3 | Native Android APIs and tooling | Android-only UI implementation | Android fidelity and platform access dominate | Compose modules and translated token names | https://developer.android.com/compose |
| Expo + @react-native-reusables/cli | React Native workflow with reusable primitives | Native edge cases may require modules | TypeScript skills and multi-platform delivery matter | React Native components and shared token names | @react-native-reusables/cli |

## Monorepo
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nx | Project graph, generators, and dependency constraints | More governance concepts | Many projects need enforceable boundaries | Publishable and buildable libraries | https://nx.dev |
| Turborepo | Simple task graph and caching | Fewer architecture constraints | Existing workspace needs lightweight orchestration | Workspace packages | https://turborepo.com/docs |
| pnpm workspaces | Minimal native workspace layer | No project graph or generators | Package linking is the main requirement | Workspace packages | https://pnpm.io/workspaces |

## Library/CLI
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Backend
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NestJS | Structured modules and dependency injection | Heavier framework conventions | Large API needs consistent layering | Modules, guards, and providers | https://docs.nestjs.com |
| Hono | Small web-standard API core | Fewer built-in enterprise patterns | Edge portability and low overhead matter | Handlers and middleware | https://hono.dev/docs |
| Fastify | Mature Node plugin ecosystem and schemas | Node-oriented runtime | Throughput and plugin composition matter | Plugins, schemas, and hooks | https://fastify.dev/docs |

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.
If matrix evidence is unavailable, PRD answers conflict, or the reason is unconfirmed, STOP with `status: unresolved` and name the missing evidence or conflicting answers. Treat selection and STOP behavior as honor-system.

## Callers and ownership

Accept calls from `greenfield-init` for new repositories and from `brownfield-audit` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting. Keep matrices and ADR decision content in this skill and `references/matrices.md`.

Return both stack ADR decisions without implementing design or token values; delegate those values to the selected design system or `zeroh-design`.

## Output

Return one `StackDecisionOutput` containing one object per applicable matrix:

```json
{"status":"decided|unresolved","decisions":[{"adrPath":"docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md|docs/adr/0002-design-system.md","matrix":"<matrix-heading>","options":["<exact-presented-row>"],"selected":"<named-option>","reason":"<confirmed-reason>","consequences":["<consequence>"],"revisitConditions":["<measurable-condition>"],"rulingDate":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]}
```

Define `YYYY-MM-DD` as the decision's ISO calendar date, `<matrix-heading>` as the literal heading in `references/matrices.md`, and every other placeholder as non-empty text copied or confirmed during selection. On STOP, return `{"status":"unresolved","decisions":[]}` plus the named conflict in the surrounding response.

Accumulate every applicable stack decision in the single
`docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md`: create a labeled Options group for each presented
matrix, preserve all of its sourced rows, and add one dated ruling per group.
Never replace an earlier group's alternatives or ruling when the next matrix is
answered. Populate `docs/adr/0002-design-system.md` separately from only the
design-system options and ruling.

Add the confirmed consequences and measurable revisit conditions for every
group. Do not write either ADR until the calling workflow's approval gate has
passed.
Treat preservation of earlier groups as honor-system. Treat the no-write rule as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` when called inside native initialization; otherwise it is honor-system.
===== matrices
# Stack matrices

Present only the applicable sections and preserve every row when asking for a choice.

## Web
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js + shadcn/ui | Integrated full-stack React and accessible primitives | Framework conventions add coupling | Product needs routing, rendering, and server seams | Registry components remain source-owned | https://nextjs.org/docs |
| Vite + React | Small, fast client toolchain | Backend and routing need separate choices | Client-rendered app has independent services | React components move between Vite applications | https://vite.dev/guide |
| SvelteKit | Concise components and integrated routing | Smaller React-library ecosystem | Team prefers Svelte and server rendering | Svelte components share within Svelte projects | https://svelte.dev/docs/kit |

## Mobile
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flutter + shadcn_flutter | One Dart UI across supported platforms | Native integrations need platform bridges | Consistent cross-platform UI is primary | Shared Dart widgets and token names | shadcn_flutter |
| Kotlin/Compose/Material 3 | Native Android APIs and tooling | Android-only UI implementation | Android fidelity and platform access dominate | Compose modules and translated token names | https://developer.android.com/compose |
| Expo + @react-native-reusables/cli | React Native workflow with reusable primitives | Native edge cases may require modules | TypeScript skills and multi-platform delivery matter | React Native components and shared token names | @react-native-reusables/cli |

## Monorepo
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nx | Project graph, generators, and dependency constraints | More governance concepts | Many projects need enforceable boundaries | Publishable and buildable libraries | https://nx.dev |
| Turborepo | Simple task graph and caching | Fewer architecture constraints | Existing workspace needs lightweight orchestration | Workspace packages | https://turborepo.com/docs |
| pnpm workspaces | Minimal native workspace layer | No project graph or generators | Package linking is the main requirement | Workspace packages | https://pnpm.io/workspaces |

## Library/CLI
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Backend
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NestJS | Structured modules and dependency injection | Heavier framework conventions | Large API needs consistent layering | Modules, guards, and providers | https://docs.nestjs.com |
| Hono | Small web-standard API core | Fewer built-in enterprise patterns | Edge portability and low overhead matter | Handlers and middleware | https://hono.dev/docs |
| Fastify | Mature Node plugin ecosystem and schemas | Node-oriented runtime | Throughput and plugin composition matter | Plugins, schemas, and hooks | https://fastify.dev/docs |

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * roadmap — the CLI that owns every repo-state transition (arc ROADCODE). Decisions
 * and transitions are CODE here; judgment stays MODEL. Plain Node ESM, one dep (zod).
 *
 * Universal exit-code contract (honesty rail — exit codes never lie):
 *   0  success / clean / the requested state holds
 *   1  usage or configuration error (missing config, unknown/args, not-yet-implemented)
 *   2  check failed / refused / red (the caller cannot narrate around it)
 *   3/4 long-poll verdicts (watch — 1657) · 5 watch UNOBSERVED (2384.2) · capacity's gate
 *   verdict is exit 3 (at capacity) · role resolve's UNJUDGED refusal is exit 2
 *
 * Commands are cli/commands/<name>.mjs default-export async run(argv) → exit code.
 * A command whose module is not present yet is listed in the tree with its owning
 * phase and exits 1 with an honest "not yet implemented" line — the skeleton shows
 * the whole tree, honestly.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { ConfigError } from '../cli/lib/config.mjs'
import { RoadmapRootError } from '../cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

// The full §2 command tree. `phase` is the owning phase and `arc` the arc that owns it
// (default ROADCODE); `sub` lists subcommands for --help. A command becomes MOUNTED the
// moment its module lands.
const TREE = {
  config: { phase: 1655, sub: ['check', 'capabilities --json'], desc: 'load bindings or report read-only protocol capabilities' },
  init: { phase: 1655, sub: ['--config', '--scaffold', '--root <dir>'], desc: 'scaffold the roadmap root + config.json' },
  status: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--json'], desc: 'derive the live lane table (absorbs arc-status.mjs)' },
  claim: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--count N'], desc: 'atomically reserve the next phase number(s)' },
  arm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--inline', '--note', '--base-ref', '--mode'], desc: 'write the .building sidecar; refuse a taken lane' },
  disarm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--paused'], desc: 'remove/pause the sidecar; clear .arc-mode; free landed claims' },
  gate: { phase: 1656, sub: ['plan <phase>', 'run <phase>'], desc: 'the gate decision table + mechanical execution' },
  result: { phase: 1656, sub: ['check'], desc: 'PhaseExecutionResult .parse() via the consumer schema' },
  contract: { phase: 1656, sub: ['show --json-schema'], desc: 'emit the PhaseExecutionResult JSON Schema' },
  arc: { phase: 1657, sub: ['next <arcId>', 'land <arcId>'], desc: 'position derivation + the ONE landing engine' },
  watch: { phase: 1657, sub: ['<arcId>', '--once'], desc: 'executor liveness (absorbs executor-watch/liveness)' },
  beacon: { phase: 1737, sub: ['<event> --phase <N>', '--detail', '--log', '--session'], desc: 'typed executor heartbeat (closed vocabulary)' },
  'executor-arm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> --session <id> [--executor-id <id>] [--agent-card <path>] [--force]'], desc: 'write the executor arm file (never unbound; refuses over another executor)' },
  'executor-disarm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> [--force]', '--sweep'], desc: 'remove an executor arm (refuses a live one) / sweep exactly the stale set' },
  phase: { phase: 1657, sub: ['validate <N|file>', 'start <N>', 'curate <N> [--apply] [--groups]', 'land <N>'], desc: 'phase-file validation, start, born-clean curation and the worktree-lane land' },
  worktree: { phase: 2146, sub: ['up', 'status', 'reset [--base <ref>]'], desc: 'the session worktree lane: claim a slot, inspect claims, reset the scratch head per phase' },
  audit: { phase: 1659, sub: ['--json'], desc: "audit-roadmap's 17 checks, mechanized" },
  followups: { phase: 2422, sub: ['census', '--json'], desc: 'census followup-file lifecycle and inbound references' },
  debt: { phase: 1658, sub: ['census', 'dispose', 'check'], desc: 'debt census/dispose wrappers' },
  measure: { phase: 1659, sub: ['--flow', '--assert'], desc: 'protocol-load meter (bytes/4 over the invocation path)' },
  capacity: { arc: 'zeroh-marketplace', phase: 11, sub: ['[--json]'], desc: 'live box-resource admission check — can another executor spawn right now (the mandatory gate for any parallel fan-out; exit 3 = at capacity)' },
  role: { arc: 'zeroh-marketplace', phase: 13, sub: ['resolve <role> [--driver <id>] [--json]'], desc: 'resolve a role to model + reach mode via the tier chain and the consumer modelPolicy (exit 2 = UNJUDGED, every tier unavailable)' },
  codex: { phase: 1838, sub: ['run <N> [<N2>…]|--arc <ID> [--worktree] [--base]', 'review <N> [<N2>…] [--doc] [--focus]', 'plan <N> --brief <path>', 'status <N>|--arc <ID> [--review|--plan]'], desc: 'detached Codex delegation lane — run implements a plan, review adversarially reads one, plan authors one from a brief (worktree + stdin prompt + journal; the driver runs the gate, the session audits and integrates)' },
  driver: { arc: 'POLYSEAT', phase: 2, sub: ['verify <id>', 'register <id>'], desc: "probe a driver's real capabilities (pasted provenance); register refuses an unverified id" },
  eval: { phase: 1996, sub: ['<ARCID> [--date] [--force] [--collect-only] [--json]', 'record-sweep --arc <ID>', 'record-verdicts --arc <ID>', 'merge-judge --arc <ID>', 'trend', 'restamp', 'lesson "<text>" [--phase N]', 'scorecard [--date] [--json]', 'propose [--json] [--dry-run]'], desc: 'arc eval: collect the trace, score the deterministic dimensions and ratchet, merge the judge verdict, record the land-time aggregates, capture a durable lesson to the committed sidecar, and cluster the corpus into ratify-only improvement proposals' },
}

function printHelp() {
  const lines = ['roadmap — phase-driven development CLI', '', 'Commands:']
  for (const [name, meta] of Object.entries(TREE)) {
    const subs = meta.sub?.length ? `  ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}` : ''
    lines.push(`  ${name.padEnd(9)}${subs.padEnd(38)} ${meta.desc}  [${meta.arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${meta.phase}]`)
  }
  lines.push('', 'Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 usage/config · 2 check failed/refused · 3/4 watch verdicts · 5 watch UNOBSERVED · capacity 3 = at capacity')
  process.stdout.write(lines.join('\n') + '\n')
}

async function main() {
  const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
  const command = argv[0]
  const rest = argv.slice(1)

  if (!command || command === '--help' || command === '-h' || command === 'help') {
    printHelp()
    return 0
  }

  // Help must never execute a state transition, even outside a consumer repo.
  if (Object.hasOwn(TREE, command) && rest.length === 1 && ['--help', '-h'].includes(rest[0])) {
    const meta = TREE[command]
    process.stdout.write(`Usage: roadmap ${command} ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}\n\n${meta.desc}\n`)
    return 0
  }

  const modUrl = new URL(`../cli/commands/${command}.mjs`, import.meta.url)
  if (existsSync(fileURLToPath(modUrl))) {
    const { default: run } = await import(modUrl)
    return await run(rest)
  }

  if (command in TREE) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `roadmap ${command}: not yet implemented (lands in ${TREE[command].arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${TREE[command].phase})\n`,
    )
    return 1
  }

  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: unknown command '${command}'. Run: roadmap --help\n`)
  return 1
}

try {
  process.exit(await main())
} catch (e) {
  // Both carry messageLines and both are REFUSALS the operator can act on — an ambiguous
  // root reached through any door (status, audit, claim, gate…) must read as one named
  // message with its remedy, never as a stack trace the reader has to decode.
  if (e instanceof ConfigError || e instanceof RoadmapRootError) {
    for (const line of e.messageLines) process.stderr.write(line + '\n')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: ${e?.stack ?? e}\n`)
  process.exit(1)
}

/**
 * roadmap-root — THE answer to "where is this consumer's roadmap?", and the ONLY module
 * under cli/ or hooks/ allowed to spell the root as a literal (cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs
 * scans for it; every other site joins onto what these functions return).
 *
 * Two homes, discovered rather than configured: the config lives INSIDE the root, so a
 * roadmap.config.json key could never name it. `roadmap/` at the git toplevel is what every
 * consumer has today and stays first; `docs/roadmap/` is the second candidate, for a repo that
 * keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders (docs/roadmap/ beside docs/superpowers/).
 *
 * The rules, in order:
 *  - ROADMAP_ROOT wins, absolute or resolved against `dir`, and is NOT probed — an override
 *    names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
 *  - else the first candidate carrying a MARKER (roadmap.config.json or phases/). An existing
 *    but unmarked directory is not a marker: a repo with a prose docs/roadmap/ folder must
 *    keep reading its real roadmap/.
 *  - both marked → RoadmapRootError('ambiguous'), never a silent pick. Two roots means two
 *    backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories; guessing one is how half a
 *    consumer's records go quietly unread.
 *  - neither marked → the default first candidate, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers
 *    exactly what it answered before this module existed.
 *
 * SHELL TWIN: hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh implements the same three rules for the hooks, which
 * cannot afford to spawn node on every tool call. A change here is a change there. It differs in
 * FORM only on ambiguity — it returns non-zero after one stderr line instead of throwing, because
 * a hook must never block a session — and in neither case does either twin GUESS a root.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, resolve, relative, isAbsolute, sep } from 'node:path'
import { BridgeError } from './bridge-error.mjs'
import { gitToplevel } from './gitroot.mjs'

/** The root homes, in PRECEDENCE order. Extending this list extends discovery everywhere. */
export const ROOT_CANDIDATES = ['roadmap', 'docs/roadmap']

/** What makes a candidate directory a roadmap root rather than a same-named prose folder. */
const MARKERS = ['roadmap.config.json', 'phases']

/** Typed root-resolution failure. kind ∈ 'ambiguous'. Same shape as ConfigError. */
export class RoadmapRootError extends Error {
  constructor(kind, messageLines) {
    super(messageLines.join('\n'))
    this.name = 'RoadmapRootError'
    this.kind = kind
    this.messageLines = messageLines
  }
}

/** [dir, override] → resolved root. Keyed on both: a memo keyed on dir alone
 *  would hand a later caller an answer the current ROADMAP_ROOT never authorized. */
const memo = new Map()

/**
 * Drop every memoized resolution. For tests and long-lived processes that MUTATE a tree
 * (scaffolding a root, then resolving it) — the probes are fs reads, and a cached miss
 * outlives the directory that caused it.
 */
export function resetRoadmapRootCache() {
  memo.clear()
}

/** The override in force, or null. An empty ROADMAP_ROOT is unset, not "the cwd". */
function override() {
  const raw = process.env.ROADMAP_ROOT
  return raw != null && raw !== '' ? raw : null
}

const isRoot = (candidateDir) => MARKERS.some((m) => existsSync(join(candidateDir, m)))

/**
 * The consumer's roadmap data root for the tree at `dir` (normally a git toplevel).
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous' when more than one candidate is marked
 */
export function roadmapRoot(dir) {
  const env = override()
  const key = JSON.stringify([dir, env])
  const hit = memo.get(key)
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit

  // The override is checked BEFORE the ambiguity refusal on purpose: it is the remedy that
  // refusal advertises, and a remedy resolved after the throw could never be taken.
  const resolved = env ? (isAbsolute(env) ? env : resolve(dir, env)) : probe(dir)
  memo.set(key, resolved)
  return resolved
}

function probe(dir) {
  const marked = ROOT_CANDIDATES.map((c) => resolve(dir, c)).filter(isRoot)
  if (marked.length > 1) {
    throw new RoadmapRootError('ambiguous', [
      `roadmap: ${dir} carries more than one roadmap root — ${marked.join(' and ')}`,
      `each holds its own records, so reading either one silently hides the other. Delete or merge the one that is not yours, or name the real root: ROADMAP_ROOT=<dir> roadmap <command>`,
    ])
  }
  return marked[0] ?? resolve(dir, ROOT_CANDIDATES[0])
}

/**
 * The root a FLAGLESS `roadmap status` / `roadmap claim` reads: the consumer's resolved root.
 * Outside a git repo — where both commands still accept a bare roadmap directory — the
 * candidate under `cwd`.
 *
 * ONLY the not-a-repo case falls back. A RoadmapRootError must ESCAPE: falling back on an
 * ambiguous tree would resolve `<cwd>/roadmap` and silently pick one of the two roots the
 * refusal exists to prevent — and from a SUBDIRECTORY it would invent a root that is not
 * there at all.
 * @param {string} cwd
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous', unchanged, from either branch
 */
export function defaultRoadmapRoot(cwd) {
  let toplevel
  try {
    toplevel = gitToplevel(cwd)
  } catch {
    return roadmapRoot(cwd)
  }
  return roadmapRoot(toplevel)
}

/**
 * The same answer spelled RELATIVE to `dir`, POSIX-separated and with no trailing slash —
 * what git pathspecs (`git log -- <rel>/backlog.ts`), diff-path prefix tests and the
 * repo-relative provenance strings cited in eval reports all need. Throws exactly where
 * roadmapRoot throws: an ambiguous tree must never be handed a guessed pathspec.
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} e.g. 'roadmap' or 'docs/roadmap'
 */
export function roadmapRootRel(dir) {
  const rel = relative(dir, roadmapRoot(dir))
  return sep === '/' ? rel : rel.split(sep).join('/')
}

/**
 * The consumer's vendored schema seam — what the tsx bridge validates every typed roadmap
 * file through. Root-first (`<root>/lib/schema.ts`, what a consumer scaffolded from now on
 * carries, reachable by a relative import with no tsconfig alias), then the LEGACY
 * `<dir>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that every existing consumer still has.
 * @param {string} dir  a consumer root (git toplevel)
 * @returns {string} an absolute path to an existing file
 * @throws {BridgeError} kind 'schema-missing', naming BOTH candidates
 */
export function consumerSchemaPath(dir) {
  const rootSeam = join(roadmapRoot(dir), 'lib', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(rootSeam)) return rootSeam
  const legacySeam = join(dir, 'lib', 'roadmap', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(legacySeam)) return legacySeam
  throw new BridgeError('schema-missing', [
    `roadmap: no consumer schema at ${rootSeam} (nor at the legacy seam ${legacySeam}) — this repo is not a roadmap consumer`,
  ])
}

/**
 * roadmap — the CLI that owns every repo-state transition (arc ROADCODE). Decisions
 * and transitions are CODE here; judgment stays MODEL. Plain Node ESM, one dep (zod).
 *
 * Universal exit-code contract (honesty rail — exit codes never lie):
 *   0  success / clean / the requested state holds
 *   1  usage or configuration error (missing config, unknown/args, not-yet-implemented)
 *   2  check failed / refused / red (the caller cannot narrate around it)
 *   3/4 long-poll verdicts (watch — 1657) · 5 watch UNOBSERVED (2384.2) · capacity's gate
 *   verdict is exit 3 (at capacity) · role resolve's UNJUDGED refusal is exit 2
 *
 * Commands are cli/commands/<name>.mjs default-export async run(argv) → exit code.
 * A command whose module is not present yet is listed in the tree with its owning

import { RoadmapRootError } from '../cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

function printHelp() {
  const lines = ['roadmap — phase-driven development CLI', '', 'Commands:']
  for (const [name, meta] of Object.entries(TREE)) {
    const subs = meta.sub?.length ? `  ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}` : ''
    lines.push(`  ${name.padEnd(9)}${subs.padEnd(38)} ${meta.desc}  [${meta.arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${meta.phase}]`)
  }
  lines.push('', 'Exit codes: 0 clean · 1 usage/config · 2 check failed/refused · 3/4 watch verdicts · 5 watch UNOBSERVED · capacity 3 = at capacity')
  process.stdout.write(lines.join('\n') + '\n')

async function main() {
  const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
  const command = argv[0]
  const rest = argv.slice(1)

  if (!command || command === '--help' || command === '-h' || command === 'help') {
    printHelp()
    return 0
  }

  // Help must never execute a state transition, even outside a consumer repo.
  if (Object.hasOwn(TREE, command) && rest.length === 1 && ['--help', '-h'].includes(rest[0])) {
    const meta = TREE[command]
    process.stdout.write(`Usage: roadmap ${command} ${meta.sub.join(' | ')}\n\n${meta.desc}\n`)
    return 0
  }

  const modUrl = new URL(`../cli/commands/${command}.mjs`, import.meta.url)
  if (existsSync(fileURLToPath(modUrl))) {
    const { default: run } = await import(modUrl)
    return await run(rest)
  }

  if (command in TREE) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `roadmap ${command}: not yet implemented (lands in ${TREE[command].arc ?? 'ROADCODE'} ${TREE[command].phase})\n`,
    )
    return 1
  }

  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: unknown command '${command}'. Run: roadmap --help\n`)
  return 1
}

try {
  process.exit(await main())
} catch (e) {
  // Both carry messageLines and both are REFUSALS the operator can act on — an ambiguous
  // root reached through any door (status, audit, claim, gate…) must read as one named
  // message with its remedy, never as a stack trace the reader has to decode.
  if (e instanceof ConfigError || e instanceof RoadmapRootError) {
    for (const line of e.messageLines) process.stderr.write(line + '\n')
    process.exit(1)
  }
  process.stderr.write(`roadmap: ${e?.stack ?? e}\n`)
  process.exit(1)
}

/**
 * roadmap-root — THE answer to "where is this consumer's roadmap?", and the ONLY module
 * under cli/ or hooks/ allowed to spell the root as a literal (cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs
 * scans for it; every other site joins onto what these functions return).
 *
 * Two homes, discovered rather than configured: the config lives INSIDE the root, so a
 * roadmap.config.json key could never name it. `roadmap/` at the git toplevel is what every
 * consumer has today and stays first; `docs/roadmap/` is the second candidate, for a repo that
 * keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders (docs/roadmap/ beside docs/superpowers/).
 *
 * The rules, in order:
 *  - ROADMAP_ROOT wins, absolute or resolved against `dir`, and is NOT probed — an override
 *    names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
 *  - else the first candidate carrying a MARKER (roadmap.config.json or phases/). An existing
 *    but unmarked directory is not a marker: a repo with a prose docs/roadmap/ folder must
 *    keep reading its real roadmap/.
 *  - both marked → RoadmapRootError('ambiguous'), never a silent pick. Two roots means two
 *    backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories; guessing one is how half a
 *    consumer's records go quietly unread.
 *  - neither marked → the default first candidate, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers
 *    exactly what it answered before this module existed.
 *
 * SHELL TWIN: hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh implements the same three rules for the hooks, which
 * cannot afford to spawn node on every tool call. A change here is a change there. It differs in
 * FORM only on ambiguity — it returns non-zero after one stderr line instead of throwing, because
 * a hook must never block a session — and in neither case does either twin GUESS a root.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, resolve, relative, isAbsolute, sep } from 'node:path'
import { BridgeError } from './bridge-error.mjs'
import { gitToplevel } from './gitroot.mjs'

/** The root homes, in PRECEDENCE order. Extending this list extends discovery everywhere. */
export const ROOT_CANDIDATES = ['roadmap', 'docs/roadmap']

/** What makes a candidate directory a roadmap root rather than a same-named prose folder. */
const MARKERS = ['roadmap.config.json', 'phases']

/** Typed root-resolution failure. kind ∈ 'ambiguous'. Same shape as ConfigError. */
export class RoadmapRootError extends Error {
  constructor(kind, messageLines) {
    super(messageLines.join('\n'))
    this.name = 'RoadmapRootError'
    this.kind = kind
    this.messageLines = messageLines
  }
}

/** [dir, override] → resolved root. Keyed on both: a memo keyed on dir alone
 *  would hand a later caller an answer the current ROADMAP_ROOT never authorized. */
const memo = new Map()

/**
 * Drop every memoized resolution. For tests and long-lived processes that MUTATE a tree
 * (scaffolding a root, then resolving it) — the probes are fs reads, and a cached miss
 * outlives the directory that caused it.
 */
export function resetRoadmapRootCache() {
  memo.clear()
}

/** The override in force, or null. An empty ROADMAP_ROOT is unset, not "the cwd". */
function override() {
  const raw = process.env.ROADMAP_ROOT
  return raw != null && raw !== '' ? raw : null
}

const isRoot = (candidateDir) => MARKERS.some((m) => existsSync(join(candidateDir, m)))

/**
 * The consumer's roadmap data root for the tree at `dir` (normally a git toplevel).
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous' when more than one candidate is marked
 */
export function roadmapRoot(dir) {
  const env = override()
  const key = JSON.stringify([dir, env])
  const hit = memo.get(key)
  if (hit !== undefined) return hit

  // The override is checked BEFORE the ambiguity refusal on purpose: it is the remedy that
  // refusal advertises, and a remedy resolved after the throw could never be taken.
  const resolved = env ? (isAbsolute(env) ? env : resolve(dir, env)) : probe(dir)
  memo.set(key, resolved)
  return resolved
}

function probe(dir) {
  const marked = ROOT_CANDIDATES.map((c) => resolve(dir, c)).filter(isRoot)
  if (marked.length > 1) {
    throw new RoadmapRootError('ambiguous', [
      `roadmap: ${dir} carries more than one roadmap root — ${marked.join(' and ')}`,
      `each holds its own records, so reading either one silently hides the other. Delete or merge the one that is not yours, or name the real root: ROADMAP_ROOT=<dir> roadmap <command>`,
    ])
  }
  return marked[0] ?? resolve(dir, ROOT_CANDIDATES[0])
}

/**
 * The root a FLAGLESS `roadmap status` / `roadmap claim` reads: the consumer's resolved root.
 * Outside a git repo — where both commands still accept a bare roadmap directory — the
 * candidate under `cwd`.
 *
 * ONLY the not-a-repo case falls back. A RoadmapRootError must ESCAPE: falling back on an
 * ambiguous tree would resolve `<cwd>/roadmap` and silently pick one of the two roots the
 * refusal exists to prevent — and from a SUBDIRECTORY it would invent a root that is not
 * there at all.
 * @param {string} cwd
 * @returns {string} an ABSOLUTE directory path
 * @throws {RoadmapRootError} kind 'ambiguous', unchanged, from either branch
 */
export function defaultRoadmapRoot(cwd) {
  let toplevel
  try {
    toplevel = gitToplevel(cwd)
  } catch {
    return roadmapRoot(cwd)
  }
  return roadmapRoot(toplevel)
}

/**
 * The same answer spelled RELATIVE to `dir`, POSIX-separated and with no trailing slash —
 * what git pathspecs (`git log -- <rel>/backlog.ts`), diff-path prefix tests and the
 * repo-relative provenance strings cited in eval reports all need. Throws exactly where
 * roadmapRoot throws: an ambiguous tree must never be handed a guessed pathspec.
 * @param {string} dir
 * @returns {string} e.g. 'roadmap' or 'docs/roadmap'
 */
export function roadmapRootRel(dir) {
  const rel = relative(dir, roadmapRoot(dir))
  return sep === '/' ? rel : rel.split(sep).join('/')
}

/**
 * The consumer's vendored schema seam — what the tsx bridge validates every typed roadmap
 * file through. Root-first (`<root>/lib/schema.ts`, what a consumer scaffolded from now on
 * carries, reachable by a relative import with no tsconfig alias), then the LEGACY
 * `<dir>/lib/roadmap/schema.ts` that every existing consumer still has.
 * @param {string} dir  a consumer root (git toplevel)
 * @returns {string} an absolute path to an existing file
 * @throws {BridgeError} kind 'schema-missing', naming BOTH candidates
 */
export function consumerSchemaPath(dir) {
  const rootSeam = join(roadmapRoot(dir), 'lib', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(rootSeam)) return rootSeam
  const legacySeam = join(dir, 'lib', 'roadmap', 'schema.ts')
  if (existsSync(legacySeam)) return legacySeam
  throw new BridgeError('schema-missing', [
    `roadmap: no consumer schema at ${rootSeam} (nor at the legacy seam ${legacySeam}) — this repo is not a roadmap consumer`,
  ])
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# capbuild — run a one-off build inside a HARD memory-capped transient cgroup.
#
# Sibling to `slot`. Where `slot` is for long-lived dev servers (soft
# MemoryHigh backpressure, detached service, shows on the pool dashboard),
# `capbuild` is for blocking one-shot builds — SPFx `heft --production`,
# webpack, big tsc — that spike many workers for a few minutes and exit.
#
# Why a separate tool: a build needs a *hard* ceiling, not soft backpressure.
# With MemoryMax set, when the build's worker pool exceeds the cap the kernel
# cgroup OOM killer fires INSIDE the build's own cgroup — the build dies with a
# clean failure, and sibling Claude sessions / dev servers are never touched.
# (On 2026-06-08 a bare `npm run build` in zeroh-spfx ran outside any cgroup
# cap; RAM+swap filled and systemd-oomd killed the fat long-lived Claude
# sessions instead of the short-lived webpack workers. This prevents that.)
#
# This is also the sanctioned way to run a TEST SUITE from the Claude Bash
# tool: the slot-test-guard hook blocks bare `npm test` / `vitest run` /
# `node --test` (no cap → can OOM/swap-thrash the box, cf. 2026-06-11) and
# tells the agent to prefix `capbuild`. There is deliberately no FORCE_BARE
# escape on the agent channel — `capbuild` IS the escape, with a hard cap.
#
# Runs in the FOREGROUND as a --pipe --wait transient service so you see output
# live and get the real exit code — and crucially, capbuild waits OUTSIDE the
# capped cgroup, so an OOM-kill of the run can be detected and surfaced as a
# failure instead of being mistaken for a clean pass.

set -uo pipefail

PROG=capbuild
# Which slice the run is accounted in. Default dev.slice (builds get the 12G
# pool's room). Override to test.slice for test runs you want bound to the
# tight ephemeral-test ceiling (4G), or via CAPBUILD_SLICE in the env.
SLICE="${CAPBUILD_SLICE:-dev.slice}"
MEM_DEFAULT=8G          # hard MemoryMax for the build cgroup
SWAP_DEFAULT=2G         # hard MemorySwapMax (don't let it thrash 15G of swap)
HEAP_DEFAULT=4096       # per-worker V8 --max-old-space-size (MB)

# A transient --user unit inherits the systemd user-manager environment, NOT the
# caller's shell — so scoping knobs (ITEST_FILES, AUDIT_LEDGER_ENABLED, …) die at
# the boundary unless explicitly forwarded. This built-in allowlist of known-safe
# consumer test knobs is auto-forwarded when set. Allowlist-ONLY by design:
# capbuild never blanket-forwards the environment, so secrets (GH_TOKEN, tokens
# in the shell) stay out of the unit. Extend per-run with CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV or
# --env — never by widening this to a wildcard.
DEFAULT_PASS_ENV="ITEST_FILES AUDIT_LEDGER_ENABLED TEST_CONCURRENCY E2E_PROJECT ALLURE"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
$PROG — run a one-off build in a hard memory-capped cgroup ($SLICE).

Usage:
  $PROG <cmd...>            Run cmd in \$PWD, capped at MemoryMax=$MEM_DEFAULT.
  $PROG --mem 8G <cmd...>   Override hard MemoryMax.
  $PROG --swap 0 <cmd...>   Override hard MemorySwapMax (0 = no swap).
  $PROG --heap 4096 <cmd>   Override per-worker NODE heap cap (MB).
  $PROG --slice test.slice <cmd...>   Account the run in a specific slice
                           (default $SLICE; or set CAPBUILD_SLICE).
  $PROG --env VAR <cmd...>       Forward caller's \$VAR into the capped unit.

content: PreToolUse:Bash says: ugrep-guard: rerouted the grep(s) in this command to GNU grep (/bin/grep -I). `grep` from the Bash tool is NOT GNU grep. Claude Code (>=2.1.117) shadows it with a shell function that re-execs its own binary as the embedded ugrep, whose POSIX engine builds a DFA up front and expands counted repetitions. Two or more counted maxima over a wide class make it track the cross product and allocate WITHOUT BOUND — ~100MB/s, no output, and no SIGPIPE to stop it because it never emits a match, so a downstream `head` will not save you. On 2026-08-22 exactly this shape (`grep -o '[^<>]\{0,120\}retry[^<>]\{0,120\}' design.html` over a minified HTML file with a 91,000-char line) reached 8.9G in ONE process, blew past the session's 8G MemoryHigh with its swap cap full, and livelocked the whole session cgroup for 40 minutes. Upstream: anthropics/claude-code#54394. Measured on that file: GNU grep 0.4s/13MB with the correct answer; ugrep unbounded. Single counted repetitions, narrow classes like [0-9], and maxima under 32 are all fine and are never touched here. Only the regex ENGINE changed, so the match result is the same; the one difference is binary files, which -I keeps skipped exactly as the shim does. Write it this way yourself next time: /bin/grep, -P, or rg.

== plugin README
# zeroh-greenfield

Approval-gated setup for new repositories and gap-only standards work for
existing ones.

## Skills

- `using-zeroh-greenfield` chooses the correct workflow.
- `greenfield-init` interviews, proposes, waits for approval, and initializes.
- `brownfield-audit` identifies and fills approved gaps without replacing homes.
- `stack-decision` records sourced stack alternatives and the chosen option.

## Claude Code

```text
/plugin marketplace add Blade-Labs/zeroh-marketplace
/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace
```

Restart Claude Code or begin a fresh session after installation so the skills are loaded.

## Codex

```text
codex plugin marketplace add Blade-Labs/zeroh-marketplace
```

Install or enable `zeroh-greenfield` from the Codex plugin marketplace, then start a fresh Codex session.

## How it relates

| Plugin | Ownership |
| --- | --- |
| zeroh-greenfield | Missing project homes |
| zeroh-roadmap | Consume pointers and run phases |
| zeroh-design | Blade tokens and themes |

The architecture and ownership decisions live in
[`roadmap/arc-prompts/GREENFIELD-execution-prompt.md`](../../roadmap/arc-prompts/GREENFIELD-execution-prompt.md).

== plugin README
# zeroh-greenfield

Approval-gated setup for new repositories and gap-only standards work for
existing ones.

## Skills

- `using-zeroh-greenfield` chooses the correct workflow.
- `greenfield-init` interviews, proposes, waits for approval, and initializes.
- `brownfield-audit` identifies and fills approved gaps without replacing homes.
- `stack-decision` records sourced stack alternatives and the chosen option.

## Claude Code

```text
/plugin marketplace add Blade-Labs/zeroh-marketplace
/plugin install zeroh-greenfield@zeroh-marketplace
```

Restart Claude Code or begin a fresh session after installation so the skills are loaded.

## Codex

```text
codex plugin marketplace add Blade-Labs/zeroh-marketplace
```

Install or enable `zeroh-greenfield` from the Codex plugin marketplace, then start a fresh Codex session.

## How it relates

| Plugin | Ownership |
| --- | --- |
| zeroh-greenfield | Missing project homes |
| zeroh-roadmap | Consume pointers and run phases |
| zeroh-design | Blade tokens and themes |

The architecture and ownership decisions live in
[`roadmap/arc-prompts/GREENFIELD-execution-prompt.md`](../../roadmap/arc-prompts/GREENFIELD-execution-prompt.md).
